scenario_text: A fintech startup wants to launch a personal loan app for young professionals. They want quick disbursal, maybe under 10 minutes. The product team is small — 3 people — and the CEO wants to launch an MVP in 2 months, then iterate based on user feedback. Requirements will definitely change as they learn what users want.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a user interface for personal loan applications accessible via mobile devices.
requirements.business_justification: Young professionals primarily access banking services via smartphones; the system must be usable on these devices to capture the target market.
requirements.assumptions: Users have compatible mobile operating systems and internet connectivity.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The application loads and functions correctly on iOS and Android devices with screen widths ranging from 320px to 1920px.
applicable_regulations: Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls (RBI/2020-21/74 DoS.CO.CSITE.SEC.No.1852/31.01.015/2020-21) [issued 18 Feb 2021; in force six months from publication]

requirements.statement: The system shall display loan eligibility and estimated disbursement timelines to the user upon application submission.
requirements.business_justification: Transparency regarding speed (e.g., 'under 10 minutes') is a key value proposition for young professionals; managing expectations reduces support queries.
requirements.assumptions: The backend credit scoring engine is operational and returns results within the specified timeframe.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: After submission, the user receives a confirmation screen displaying the estimated disbursement time (e.g., '10 minutes') within 5 seconds of API response.

requirements.statement: The system shall integrate with external credit bureaus and identity verification services to assess applicant risk.
requirements.business_justification: Lending decisions require accurate credit assessment to mitigate default risk and comply with lending regulations.
requirements.assumptions: External APIs for credit scoring and identity verification are available and stable.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system successfully retrieves a credit score and identity verification status from the configured external providers within 30 seconds of request.
applicable_regulations: Local Lending Regulations
Data Privacy Laws

requirements.statement: The system shall store and process user data in compliance with applicable data protection regulations.
requirements.business_justification: Failure to protect personal financial data leads to legal penalties, reputational damage, and loss of customer trust.
requirements.assumptions: The system architecture supports encryption at rest and in transit.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: All personally identifiable information (PII) is encrypted using AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit; access logs are maintained for audit trails.
applicable_regulations: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 §2 (Act No. 22 of 2023) [as enacted]
Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 §5(iii) (Act No. 22 of 2023) [as enacted]
Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 §17(b) (Act No. 22 of 2023) [as enacted]

requirements.statement: The system shall allow the product team to modify loan terms, interest rates, and approval thresholds without requiring a code deployment.
requirements.business_justification: Requirements will change as the MVP iterates; the system must support agile configuration changes to adapt quickly to user feedback.
requirements.assumptions: A configuration management module exists within the system architecture.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: An authorized admin can update a loan interest rate parameter in the admin dashboard, and the change takes effect for new applications within 1 minute without restarting services.

requirements.statement: The system shall log all user actions and system events for audit and fraud detection purposes.
requirements.business_justification: Financial systems require immutable logs to investigate fraud, ensure accountability, and meet regulatory audit requirements.
requirements.assumptions: A centralized logging infrastructure is available.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Every user action (login, application submit, approval) generates an immutable log entry containing timestamp, user ID, IP address, and action type, stored for a minimum of 7 years.

requirements.statement: The system shall handle application submissions asynchronously to ensure quick response times even under high load.
requirements.business_justification: To meet the 'quick disbursal' promise and prevent timeouts during peak usage, the system must decouple request processing from immediate user feedback.
requirements.assumptions: The backend processing (credit check, approval) takes longer than the frontend response time.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system returns a 'Submission Successful' message to the user within 2 seconds of clicking submit, even if the full credit check takes up to 60 seconds.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a mechanism for users to view their application status and receive notifications on approval or rejection.
requirements.business_justification: Users need visibility into the progress of their loan request to reduce anxiety and support inquiries.
requirements.assumptions: The system supports push notifications or email/SMS gateways.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Users can view real-time status (e.g., 'Under Review', 'Approved') in their profile, and receive an SMS notification 1 minute after a final decision is made.

requirements.statement: The system shall allow users to cancel an active loan application within a configurable time window (e.g., 5 minutes) after submission without incurring fees.
requirements.business_justification: Users may change their minds immediately after seeing eligibility; MVP iteration requires flexible cancellation policies to reduce friction and improve conversion rates.

requirements.statement: The system shall display a clear error message and retry option to the user if an external credit bureau or identity service times out or returns a 5xx error.
requirements.business_justification: External services are prone to latency; without explicit handling, users will abandon the app during the critical 'quick disbursal' window.
applicable_regulations: Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls §35 (RBI/2020-21/74 DoS.CO.CSITE.SEC.No.1852/31.01.015/2020-21) [issued 18 Feb 2021; in force six months from publication]

requirements.statement: The system shall provide an admin dashboard for the 3-person product team to view real-time application counts, average processing time, and error rates per external service.
requirements.business_justification: With a small team and rapid iteration goals, operations staff need immediate visibility into bottlenecks to make data-driven decisions without waiting for reports.

requirements.statement: The system shall automatically archive completed loan applications and associated documents after a configurable retention period (e.g., 7 years) while keeping active application data in the hot store.
requirements.business_justification: To manage database costs and performance for an MVP, inactive data must be moved to cold storage or archived without manual intervention.
applicable_regulations: The Aadhaar (Authentication and Offline Verification) Regulations, 2021 §27 (No. 2 of 2021 (K-11020/240/2021/Auth/UIDAI)) [updated 15 Dec 2025]

requirements.statement: The system shall allow users to upload alternative documents (e.g., bank statements) if the initial identity verification fails due to a low-quality photo or mismatched data.
requirements.business_justification: Young professionals may have varying document formats; failing immediately on one check reduces conversion, so a correction path is essential for usability.

requirements.statement: The system shall enforce rate limiting on the application submission endpoint to prevent abuse and ensure fair access during high-load scenarios.
requirements.business_justification: Quick disbursal under 10 minutes implies high concurrency; without rate limiting, a few bad actors could degrade performance for legitimate users.

requirements.statement: The system shall support dark mode and meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA contrast ratios for users with visual impairments.
requirements.business_justification: Accessibility is a core usability requirement for modern fintech apps; excluding visually impaired users limits market reach and violates inclusive design principles.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a 'correction' button on the application status page allowing users to resubmit missing or incorrect documents without restarting the entire workflow.
requirements.business_justification: Users often make minor mistakes during input; a dedicated correction mechanism reduces support tickets and improves completion rates.

issues.description: The term 'configured external providers' is vague. The requirement does not specify which specific credit bureaus or identity verification services are supported, making it impossible to verify compliance with the acceptance criteria without knowing the configuration scope.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'configured external providers' with a reference to a specific list of approved vendors (e.g., 'CIBIL, Experian, Equifax') or a defined configuration file name.

issues.description: The phrase 'without requiring a code deployment' is vague. It does not define the mechanism (e.g., hot-swappable config, feature flags) or the maximum time allowed for the change to propagate after an admin action.
issues.suggestion: Specify the propagation time (e.g., 'within 1 minute') and the method of update (e.g., 'via configuration management system') instead of relying on the vague phrase.

issues.description: The requirement mentions storing logs for 'fraud detection' and cites regulations but fails to explicitly state that the log entries must be protected against tampering (e.g., 'stored in a write-once-read-many medium', 'signed with a private key', or 'immutable storage').
issues.suggestion: Add specific technical controls for immutability, such as 'Logs shall be written to an immutable storage system (e.g., WORM)' or 'Logs shall be cryptographically signed upon creation'.

issues.description: The requirement involves sending 'notifications' (SMS/Email) regarding loan status, which constitutes sensitive financial data transmission. It lacks requirements for encryption in transit for these notifications and does not mention authentication mechanisms to prevent interception.
issues.suggestion: Add acceptance criteria stating: 'SMS and email notifications containing application status shall be transmitted over encrypted channels (e.g., TLS 1.3 for email, carrier-grade encryption for SMS) and must not contain sensitive PII beyond the status update.'

issues.description: The term 'configurable time window' is vague and unmeasurable. The requirement states '(e.g., 5 minutes)' but does not mandate this specific value or define how the configuration is managed.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'configurable time window (e.g., 5 minutes)' with a concrete, measurable constraint such as 'within 5 minutes' if that is the MVP target, or specify the exact mechanism for configuration.
Identify and populate the 'stakeholder' field with the specific team or department (e.g., Product Owner, Risk Team) responsible for this requirement.

issues.description: The requirement lacks a concrete, measurable definition for 'rate limiting'. It does not specify the limit value (e.g., requests per minute), the scope (per IP, per user ID), or the action taken upon exceeding the limit.
issues.suggestion: Specify the exact rate limit parameters (e.g., 'limit to 10 submissions per hour per IP address') and the enforcement mechanism.

risk_register.title: Borrower given a Key Facts Statement before the loan contract
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025 §8 (RBI/2025-26/36 DOR.STR.REC.19/21.07.001/2025-26) [issued 08 May 2025 (para 6 from 01 Nov 2025, para 17 from 15 Jun 2025)])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall present the borrower with a Key Facts Statement (APR, repayment schedule, all charges) before the loan contract is executed.

risk_register.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery for the system
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices §28 (RBI/2023-24/107) [issued 07 Nov 2023])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall have a disaster recovery arrangement with defined recovery time and recovery point objectives, tested periodically under the bank's business continuity plan.

risk_register.title: Cooling-off period to exit a digital loan without penalty
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025 §10 (RBI/2025-26/36 DOR.STR.REC.19/21.07.001/2025-26) [issued 08 May 2025 (para 6 from 01 Nov 2025, para 17 from 15 Jun 2025)])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall let a borrower exit a digital loan during a cooling-off period of at least one day by repaying the principal and proportionate APR, without penalty.

risk_register.title: Cyber incidents reported to CERT-In within 6 hours
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall support reporting cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of their being noticed, with a copy to the sector regulator.

risk_register.title: Cyber security incidents reported promptly to RBI
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Cyber Security Framework in Banks §15 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall detect and log cyber security incidents and support reporting them to RBI (and CERT-In) within the mandated timelines.

risk_register.title: Digital lending data stored only on servers in India
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025 §13 (RBI/2025-26/36 DOR.STR.REC.19/21.07.001/2025-26) [issued 08 May 2025 (para 6 from 01 Nov 2025, para 17 from 15 Jun 2025)])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall store all borrower and loan data only on servers located in India.

risk_register.title: Frauds reported to RBI through the fraud monitoring return within 14 days of classification
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Directions on Fraud Risk Management in Commercial Banks (including RRBs) and AIFIs §6.3 (RBI/2024-25 Fraud Risk Management) [revised 2024])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall generate the fraud monitoring return for each case classified as fraud so that it can be reported to RBI within 14 days of classification.

risk_register.title: ICT system logs kept for a rolling 180 days within India
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(iv) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall keep logs of all its ICT components securely for a rolling 180 days, within India, and make them available to CERT-In on request.

risk_register.title: Lending app does not access contacts, call logs or media; device access only with explicit consent
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025 §12 (RBI/2025-26/36 DOR.STR.REC.19/21.07.001/2025-26) [issued 08 May 2025 (para 6 from 01 Nov 2025, para 17 from 15 Jun 2025)])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The lending app shall not access the borrower's files and media, contact list, call logs or telephony functions; camera, microphone and location may be accessed once, for onboarding/KYC only, with explicit consent recorded in an audit trail.

risk_register.title: Loans disbursed only into the borrower's own bank account, never via a third party
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025 §9 (RBI/2025-26/36 DOR.STR.REC.19/21.07.001/2025-26) [issued 08 May 2025 (para 6 from 01 Nov 2025, para 17 from 15 Jun 2025)])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall disburse loans only into the borrower's own bank account and never through any third-party or lending-service-provider account.

risk_register.title: Personal data breaches notified to the Data Protection Board and affected individuals
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 §8(b) (Act No. 22 of 2023) [as enacted])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall support detection of personal data breaches and notification of each breach to the Data Protection Board and every affected customer in the prescribed form and time.

risk_register.title: Personal data processed only with the data principal's consent (or another lawful ground)
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 §4 (Act No. 22 of 2023) [as enacted])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall obtain and record the customer's consent for each specified purpose before processing their personal data, and allow the consent to be withdrawn as easily as it was given.

risk_register.title: Transaction records kept at least five years from the date of transaction
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Direction — Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016 §(a) (RBI/DBR/2015-16/18) [updated 14 Aug 2025])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall retain records of all transactions with the customer for at least five years from the date of the transaction.

risk_register.title: Requirements expected to change
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "The product team is small — 3 people — and the CEO wants to launch an MVP in 2 months, then iterate based on user feedback."
risk_register.consequence: Work built early is discarded as the scope moves.
risk_register.mitigation: Deliver in short increments and keep the backlog prioritised with the product owner.
evidence: The product team is small — 3 people — and the CEO wants to launch an MVP in 2 months, then iterate based on user feedback.

risk_register.title: A grievance redressal mechanism for customers
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Direction on Outsourcing of Information Technology Services §7 (RBI/2023-24/102) [issued 10 Apr 2023])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall let customers raise complaints and disputes, track them to resolution, and show the contact details of the designated grievance redressal officer.

risk_register.title: Notice to the data principal stating what personal data is collected and why
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 §5 (Act No. 22 of 2023) [as enacted])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall present a notice, before or at the time of collection, stating the personal data collected, the purpose of processing and how the customer can exercise their rights and complain.

risk_register.title: Personal data erased when consent is withdrawn or the purpose is served — unless law requires retention
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 §8(a) (Act No. 22 of 2023) [as enacted])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall erase a customer's personal data when consent is withdrawn or the purpose is no longer served, except where retention is required by law (such as the five-year KYC record retention), and record the basis for any retention.

risk_register.title: System clocks synchronised to NIC/NPL time servers
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(i) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall synchronise all its clocks to the NIC or NPL NTP servers (or servers traceable to them), so that log timestamps are reliable.

risk_register.title: Unverified regulation on REQ-003
risk_register.cause: REQ-003 names Local Lending Regulations, Data Privacy Laws, which nothing in the knowledge base supports.
risk_register.consequence: The design rests on a regulation nobody has checked applies, or exists in that form.
risk_register.mitigation: Have compliance confirm the named regulation and its applicable clause.

risk_register.title: Contradictory requirements REQ-009 / REQ-012
risk_register.cause: Possible conflict: the two statements state different values for duration. The judge read it as overlap: REQ-009 defines behavior for 'active' applications (cancellation), while REQ-012 defines behavior for 'completed' applications (archiving). These are related but distinct scopes within the same lifecycle domain; satisfying one does not automatically satisfy the other. (unconfirmed)
risk_register.consequence: One of the two requirements will be built wrong and reworked.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm with the stakeholders which statement is correct.

risk_register.title: Missing security/compliance in REQ-006
risk_register.cause: The requirement mentions storing logs for 'fraud detection' and cites regulations but fails to explicitly state that the log entries must be protected against tampering (e.g., 'stored in a write-once-read-many medium', 'signed with a private key', or 'immutable storage').
risk_register.consequence: The requirement cannot be built or tested as written.
risk_register.mitigation: Add specific technical controls for immutability, such as 'Logs shall be written to an immutable storage system (e.g., WORM)' or 'Logs shall be cryptographically signed upon creation'.

risk_register.title: Missing security/compliance in REQ-008
risk_register.cause: The requirement involves sending 'notifications' (SMS/Email) regarding loan status, which constitutes sensitive financial data transmission. It lacks requirements for encryption in transit for these notifications and does not mention authentication mechanisms to prevent interception.
risk_register.consequence: The requirement cannot be built or tested as written.
risk_register.mitigation: Add acceptance criteria stating: 'SMS and email notifications containing application status shall be transmitted over encrypted channels (e.g., TLS 1.3 for email, carrier-grade encryption for SMS) and must not contain sensitive PII beyond the status update.'

risk_register.title: Small team — key-person dependency
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "The product team is small — 3 people — and the CEO wants to launch an MVP in 2 months, then iterate based on user feedback."
risk_register.consequence: Losing one person stalls the project.
risk_register.mitigation: Pair on critical components, document as you go, and identify a backup for each area.
evidence: The product team is small — 3 people — and the CEO wants to launch an MVP in 2 months, then iterate based on user feedback.

risk_register.title: Integrations authenticated, encrypted and rate-limited
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (practice: Industry practice (OWASP API Security Top 10)).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: Every integration with an external system shall be mutually authenticated, encrypted in transit, allow-listed and rate-limited, with failures logged.

risk_register.title: High-risk function depends on an external system (REQ-003)
risk_register.cause: REQ-003 is high risk and classified Integration: The system shall integrate with external credit bureaus and identity verification services to assess applicant risk.
risk_register.consequence: An external system's availability, contract or interface change blocks a high-risk function.
risk_register.mitigation: Agree interface contracts early, stub the dependency for testing, and define fallback behaviour.

risk_register.title: Fixed deadline
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "The product team is small — 3 people — and the CEO wants to launch an MVP in 2 months, then iterate based on user feedback."
risk_register.consequence: Scope is cut or quality slips to hold the date.
risk_register.mitigation: Agree what is in the first release, track it weekly, and protect testing time.
evidence: The product team is small — 3 people — and the CEO wants to launch an MVP in 2 months, then iterate based on user feedback.

risk_register.title: Insufficient team capacity for rapid iteration
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "The product team is small — 3 people"
risk_register.consequence: A three-person team may lack the necessary bandwidth to handle both the initial MVP build and the subsequent iterative cycles required by the 'learn and iterate' strategy, causing delivery delays or burnout.
risk_register.mitigation: Review with the project manager.
evidence: The product team is small — 3 people

risk_register.title: Scope creep due to iterative development model
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "Requirements will definitely change as they learn what users want."
risk_register.consequence: The project may fail to meet the fixed 2-month deadline because the scope is expected to expand or shift significantly during the MVP phase, leading to missed market windows or budget overruns.
risk_register.mitigation: Review with the project manager.
evidence: Requirements will definitely change as they learn what users want.

risk_register.title: Unrealistic performance target for complex fintech logic
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "They want quick disbursal, maybe under 10 minutes."
risk_register.consequence: Achieving sub-10-minute loan disbursement involves significant backend complexity (credit checks, fraud screening, bank integrations); setting this as a hard target for an MVP with a small team creates a high risk of technical failure or system instability.
risk_register.mitigation: Review with the project manager.
evidence: They want quick disbursal, maybe under 10 minutes.

risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (practice: OWASP ASVS (industry practice; not in the knowledge base)).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall validate all input on the server side and be built and tested against the OWASP Application Security Verification Standard.

risk_register.title: Only the personal data necessary for the stated purpose is collected
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 §6 (Act No. 22 of 2023) [as enacted]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall collect only the personal data necessary for each specified purpose and reject or discard fields not required for it.

risk_register.title: Security events monitored and alerted on
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §19.6(b) (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall forward security events to the bank's security operations monitoring and raise alerts on anomalous access or activity.

risk_register.title: Vulnerability management, patching and security testing before release
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §7.1 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall undergo vulnerability assessment and penetration testing before go-live and after major changes, and its components shall be patched under the bank's patch management policy.
